title: Reduction of the completion unit on any small Noetherian coefficient site
statement: Let S be a small site [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison], A a commutative Noetherian ring, and I an ideal. Let R be its prescribed strict quotient reduction, C its total-derived-limit completion, and eta its specified quotient unit. The natural transformation R(eta): R → C ⋙ R is invertible on every unbounded derived A-module sheaf, with no completeness assumption on its input. No torsion, finite quotient or perfect quotient hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 099M and 099N(3),(4); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0B56, 0941 and 0A07; strict-diagram refinement of fix-lem-exchanges Step 5.

proof.text: An object over A/I^(n+1) is complete after restriction: each element of I acts nilpotently, its sequential localization is zero, and internal Hom from it is zero. Apply the restriction-section and constant-element completeness criteria. This includes I=0, I=A and the zero ring.

source.place: Tags 099M and 099N(3),(4); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0B56, 0941 and 0A07; strict-diagram refinement of fix-lem-exchanges Step 5.

proof.text: Noetherianity provides finite generators of I. The normalized Koszul/quotient reflector gives Hom(CN,Res M) ≃ Hom(N,Res M). Transport across the finite scalar-extension adjunction. Coyoneda shows F_n(eta_N) is invertible. This is the finite-reduction argument with its unused extra datum assumptions removed.

source.place: Tags 099M and 099N(3),(4); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0B56, 0941 and 0A07; strict-diagram refinement of fix-lem-exchanges Step 5.

proof.text: The finite-evaluation isomorphism identifies evaluation of R(eta_N) with restriction of F_n(eta_N). These are isomorphisms. Apply evaluation/homology comparison, levelwise isomorphism detection in the strict tower abelian category, and the derived homology criterion to conclude R(eta_N) is invertible. Componentwise invertibility gives the natural isomorphism.
